earnings.title: Royal Gold Reports Strong Third Quarter Results, Including Record Operating Cash Flow and Gold Equivalent Ounce Sales, Additional Share Repurchases and Full Repayment of Debt after Quarter End
highlights: Revenue of $464.8 million (compared to $252.1 million in the prior year period)
Revenue split by commodity: 73% gold, 14% silver, 10% copper
Net income of $227.4 million ($2.68 per share), and adjusted net income 1 of $238.3 million ($2.80 per share) (compared to $126.8 million and $136.2 million, respectively, in the prior year period)
Record operating cash flow of $344.4 million (compared to $174.0 million in the prior year period)
Paid quarterly dividend of $0.475 per share, a 6% increase over the prior year period

quotes.text: Strong third quarter results extended the positive momentum from the first half of the year.
quotes.by: Bill Heissenbuttel, President and CEO of Royal Gold

outlook: During the third quarter, and in accordance with the previously announced $500 million share repurchase program approved by the Board of Directors on May 4, 2026, we repurchased 190,045 shares at an average price of $259.83 per share, for total consideration of $49 million.

items.heading: Our revenue is subject to volatility in metal prices, which could adversely affect our results of operations and cash flow.
Our acquisitions and other transactions may not result in anticipated returns or may not otherwise ultimately benefit our business.
Our future success depends on our ability to acquire additional stream or royalty interests at appropriate valuations.

For some properties, we may not realize all of the expected benefits of our investments if operators are unable to replace current mineral reserves as they are consumed or identify new mineral resources, which could adversely affect our future results of operations.

A significant portion of our revenue comes from a small number of operating properties, and adverse developments at these properties could have a more significant or lasting effect on our results of operations than if our revenue were less concentrated.
We depend on the services of our directors, executives and other key employees, and the loss of one or more of these individuals could harm our business.
